requirements.reason: Refund fulfillment jobs must use immutable attempt identity, bounded retry and exhaustion behavior, monotonic provider outcomes, and finite user notice context.
Admin retry and reconciliation must preserve amount, identity, transaction, compensation, MoneyIssue, replacement, audit, and terminal-attempt invariants.
Refund provider reads and mutations must occur outside database lock transactions and only after durable intent checkpoints commit.
Only authoritative financial workflows may write refund and credit booking summaries, with one correctly attributed history transition per committed change.
Financial outcome and refund actions must retain staff authorization, recent-auth, idempotency, audit, and minimized response contracts.
Broad reconciliation, disputes, final deployed worker capacity, live Stripe evidence, alert delivery, and operational runbooks remain later-owned.
